thread:
eva: heads-up — getting ticket from Acero showing p95->p99 tail for orchidflux-v2 after yesterday's tokenizer normalization change. customer sees 200ms -> 1700ms on long inputs (~12k tokens).

maria: ticket 8912 — they attached a sample request + request_id=req_0a9f. error rate small (~0.5%) but latency tail huge. they reported occasional 502 as well.

raj: confirmed in prod metrics — model shard 7 shows KV cache misses spike. timeline aligns with deploy at 2024-09-21T03:12Z (tokenizer normalization flags flipped).

ben: repro in staging: ran the provided 12k token prompt against orchidflux-v2 on a 80-token stride, p95 220ms, p99 1.4s. switching tokenizer back to legacy normalizer restores p99 ~280ms.

maria: customer wants ETA. also asked if billing impacted — they saw higher token counts (subtoken blow-up) for some CJK mixed input.

eva: possible causes: (1) tokenizer variant producing longer token sequences -> more KV/attention; (2) cache invalidation due to subtle token boundary changes; (3) routing to lower-capacity shard.

raj: logs: pasted snippet from runtime.

raj: ```
2024-09-21T03:20:11Z shard=7 req=req_0a9f stage=decode tokens=12103 kv_hit=false latency_ms=1420
2024-09-21T03:20:11Z shard=7 req=req_0a9f kvcache_evict=true reason=prefix_mismatch
2024-09-21T03:20:11Z shard=3 req=req_0a9f stage=route fallback=true latency_ms=1350
```

ben: interesting — route shows fallback to shard 3 (lower perf). we have a misroute event when tokenizer variant differs from model pin.

maria: customer says they set model=orchidflux-v2 (pinned) on API call. can routing override pinned model?

eva: usually no, but we have a compatibility fallback: if serving node detects incompatible tokenizer model hash it will redirect to a compatible variant. that fallback logic was widened in the normalization rollout.

raj: short repro steps for eng: curl to hit same codepath:

raj: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"orchidflux-v2","input":"<12k-token-sample>","max_tokens":256}' \
  -o /tmp/out.json -w "\nHTTP:%{http_code} TIME:%{time_total}\n"
```

ben: I reproduced with `REDWOOD_ENV=staging` and toggled env TOKEN_NORMALIZER=v2/v1. v2 -> p99 spike. v1 -> stable.

maria: for the billing question — tokenizer v2 emits more subtokens for mixed CJK+emoji. billing team: possible upward billing blips for affected customers.
